newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Clues sought to Pearson future.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Clues sought to Pearson future.

text.p: Share analysts are looking for guidance on possible disposals and the future focus of British media and leisure group Pearson Plc when it publishes its 1996 results on Monday.
The results provide a platform for new Pearson chief executive Marjorie Scardino, who took the reins in January, to outline her vision for a group which has long been accused of lacking focus.
Analysts will also seek more information on the accounting problem at Penguin USA which Pearson has said may lead to a charge against 1996 profits of as much as 100 million stg.
Pre-tax profits, excluding the Penguin provision, are expected to come in somewhere between 226-290 million stg, the wide range reflecting the numerous exceptional factors.

Pre-tax profit in 1995 was 365.1 million stg, lifted by a one-off gain on the sale of a stake in satellite broadcaster BSkyB. However, analysts will compare the 1996 number with an adjusted 1995 figure of 235.7 million.
Scardino, a Texan who came to the top job at Pearson from its 50-percent owned Economist magazine, has said that the group's performance is not good enough.
Pearson has a portfolio of stellar assets including the Financial Times newspaper, television production businesses, a 50 percent share in merchant bank Lazard Brothers and Madame Tussaud's waxworks.
Analysts believe that the invesment banking interests or the tourist attractions in its Tussauds Group could be sacrificied as part of the new management's drive for focus.
